A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in Mediterranean evergreens, TAA increases with the seasonal increase of the environmental oxidative stress and sHsps are accumulated in response to both the seasonal increase of environmental stress and to the endogenous stress of organ senescence.
the Mediterranean tree Q. ilex has a well-developed GAS that is based on the accumulation of small Hsps in stems and leaves.
the accumulation of s-Hsps in leaves of Q. ilex L. is related to the general adaptation syndrome and not to the recovery process of leaves after exposure to stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sHsps play an important role in the GAS of woody evergreens and that the accumulation of these proteins in stems is related to the lignification and suberization of tissues.

the expression of sHs proteins and the increase in TAA are two components of the general adaptive response of woody Mediterranean trees to seasonal variations and that they are not related to diurnal changes in photosynthetic activity or to the current state of leaf development.
sHsps are involved in the general adaptation response to stress in Q. ilex and that they are also involved in the maintenance of physiological functions in the absence of stress.
